hits.hook: Introducing: Browser Use 1.0.0: CDP is all you need 👀
hits.text:
Introducing: Browser Use 1.0.0: CDP is all you need 👀

We deleted 90% of the old library. Predefined state and action space make it worse.

Now the agent just writes Python REPL on raw CDP.  Simplicity wins.

> same models, up to 50% better
> 2-5x cheaper
> 2-3x faster
> SOTA https://t.co/iEtHzvljIH
hits.video_tip: Hold the chart/screenshot 3s, hard-cut zoom on the headline number.
hits.original_en:
Introducing: Browser Use 1.0.0: CDP is all you need 👀

We deleted 90% of the old library. Predefined state and action space make it worse.

Now the agent just writes Python REPL on raw CDP.  Simplicity wins.

> same models, up to 50% better
> 2-5x cheaper
> 2-3x faster
> SOTA
hits.draft_en:
Browser Use 1.0.0 just shipped, and the thesis is blunt: raw CDP is enough.

They stripped 90% of the old library. Locked-in state and action maps, they argue, made agents worse, not better.

Now each agent writes a Python REPL against raw CDP. Simplicity is the point.

They keep the same models and say quality is up to 50% better, with a 2-5x drop in cost and a 2-3x jump in speed. They are calling it SOTA.

hits.draft_en:
Muse Ember went onto a brutal long-horizon browser bench, and the cost is the story.

A run with hundreds of browser steps is priced in CENTS instead of USD, sitting on the pareto frontier.

The score is 63.9/100, tied with GPT-6 Luna medium. A task costs 3 cents, which they call 2.4x cheaper, and it posts the best mark under 5 cents.

congrats @alexandr_wang

virals.draft_en:

x_keywords.method: Read-only x MCP search_posts_all, 2 calls per keyword: last 24 h and previous 24 h (24-48 h ago); lang:en, no retweets/replies, sort=relevancy, up to 25 posts per window. This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time. Rank = sum of sampled 24 h views; 48 h = both windows; trend = 24 h sum / previous 24 h sum (up >=1.3, down <=0.7). Fresh posts are still gaining views, so 'up' is understated. Top-post share > 70% means one viral post carries the keyword.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
